relations.subject: F. B. J. Kuiper
relations.evidence: Between 1939 and 1972, he was professor of Sanskrit at Leiden University. He served as chair of the Balto-Slavic languages, taking on the role in 1941.

relations.subject: F. B. J. Kuiper
relations.evidence: beginning his studies in classical literature and Indo-European linguistics at Leiden University the same year.

relations.subject: F. B. J. Kuiper
relations.evidence: He further studied Sanskrit at the University of Utrecht under the tutelage of Willem Caland

relations.subject: F. B. J. Kuiper
relations.evidence: He further studied Sanskrit at the University of Utrecht under the tutelage of Willem Caland, taking private lessons with him at Caland's home

relations.subject: F. B. J. Kuiper
relations.evidence: Kuiper continued his studies in classical literature at Leiden. There, he studied under C. C. Uhlenbeck

relations.subject: F. B. J. Kuiper
relations.evidence: following Uhlenbeck's retirement, he began studying under Nicolaas van Wijk, a profound influence on Kuiper's work

relations.subject: F. B. J. Kuiper
relations.evidence: In 1934, Kuiper completed his doctoraalexamen, which granted him the equivalent of a master's degree, in classical literature; just two weeks later, he successfully defended his dissertation, receiving his doctorate cum laude.

relations.subject: F. B. J. Kuiper
relations.evidence: he taught classics at the Carpentier Alting Foundation Lyceum (Dutch: Lyceum der Carpentier Alting–Stichting).

relations.subject: F. B. J. Kuiper
relations.role: Regular Professor of Sanskrit and Its Literature and Indian Archeology
relations.evidence: Kuiper was appointed by Leiden University to take over the Sanskrit professorship after J. Ph. Vogel's departure

relations.subject: F. B. J. Kuiper
relations.evidence: Following Van Wijk's death, Kuiper was appointed to take over as chair of the Balto-Slavic languages.

relations.subject: F. B. J. Kuiper
relations.evidence: In 1957, he co-founded the academic journal Indo-Iranian Journal with his former student J. W. de Jong

relations.subject: J. W. de Jong
relations.evidence: In 1957, he co-founded the academic journal Indo-Iranian Journal with his former student J. W. de Jong

relations.subject: J. W. de Jong
relations.evidence: his former student J. W. de Jong

relations.subject: E. J. Furnée
relations.evidence: retiring in 1972 after his student E. J. Furnée achieved his doctorate in March.

relations.subject: Robert S. P. Beekes
relations.evidence: laid the groundwork for his student Robert S. P. Beekes's 1969 doctoral dissertation, The Development of the Proto-Indo-European Laryngeals in Greek

relations.subject: M. C. Monna
relations.evidence: and later influenced Beekes's own student, M. C. Monna.

relations.subject: Henk Bodewitz
relations.evidence: Kuiper returned as editor-in-chief for one issue in 1990, with Henk Bodewitz taking over thereafter.

relations.subject: F. B. J. Kuiper
relations.evidence: Kuiper was also at one point the director of the Kern Institute

relations.subject: Michael Witzel
relations.evidence: Following his death, Michael Witzel described him as "my last Guru"

relations.subject: Tatyana Elizarenkova
relations.evidence: Tatyana Elizarenkova, a close colleague of Kuiper's, echoed this sentiment
